title: Tenali Rama and the thieves.
lines: Long ago in the south of India there lived a clever man.
His name was Tenali Rama.
He lived in the city of Vijayanagara and he was a friend of the king.
The king often asked him for advice, because Tenali Rama was very good at thinking.
He always found a clever solution.
It was summer.
It was very hot and it hadn't rained for a long time.
Behind Tenali Rama's house was a big garden.
There were mango trees and banana plants and beautiful flowers.
But everything was dry.
The flowers were drooping.
The leaves were turning yellow.
Every day Tenali Rama had to fetch water from the deep well in his garden.
Bucket after bucket.
It was hard work.
One evening Tenali Rama was sitting on the veranda with his wife.
It was dark.
The crickets were chirping.
Suddenly Tenali Rama saw something moving behind the bushes.
He looked carefully.
It was three men.
They were whispering to each other.
Thieves!
thought Tenali Rama.
They want to break into our house tonight!
His wife got scared.
What shall we do?
she whispered.
Tenali Rama smiled.
He already had a plan.
He began to talk very loudly, so the thieves could hear.
Dear wife, he said loudly, there are lots of thieves in the city.
I'm afraid they'll come and steal our gold.
You know what?
We'll put all our gold and jewels in the big chest.
And then we'll throw the chest into the well.
Nobody will ever find it there!
His wife didn't understand at all.
But Tenali Rama winked.
Then she understood.
They went inside together.
They filled a big, heavy chest with stones.
Lots and lots of stones.
Then they carried the chest outside.
Pfff, our gold is so heavy, said Tenali Rama loudly.
And splash!
He threw the chest into the deep well.
Then they went inside and turned off the light.
But they didn't sleep.
They secretly watched through the window.
The three thieves came out.
Ha ha!
they whispered.
The gold is in the well!
They lowered a bucket into the well and began to pull up water.
Bucket after bucket after bucket.
They threw the water to the side, into the garden.
They had to empty the well to reach the chest.
They worked all night.
They sweated and sighed.
Their arms hurt.
The water flowed across the ground, past the mango trees, past the banana plants and past the flowers.
When the sun came up, the well was almost empty.
At last the thieves saw the chest.
They pulled it up and opened it.
Stones!
Nothing but stones!
At that moment Tenali Rama stepped outside.
Good morning, friends!
he said kindly.
Thank you for watering my whole garden!
The thieves looked around.
The whole garden was wet.
The flowers were standing up straight again.
The leaves were shiny.
The thieves were ashamed and quickly ran away.
They never came back.
That day Tenali Rama told the story to the king.
The king laughed so hard that his crown almost fell off.
Tenali Rama, he said, you really are the cleverest man in my kingdom!
You didn't fight and you didn't hurt anyone.
You just thought hard.
And do you know what the lesson is?
Sometimes you can do more with your head than with your hands.
The end.
